title: Rate limiter
intro: You are building the check behind an API's rate limit: each request is `(user, time)` and the limiter says whether it is allowed. Times are whole seconds and arrive in non-decreasing order. Use only the standard library. Each level extends the previous one, as a new class with the same `allow(user, t)` method.
rules: `allow(user, t)` returns True (the request is allowed and counted) or False (rejected). A rejected request is never counted.
Users are independent: one user's requests never affect another's limit.

levels.title: Fixed window per user
levels.prompt: Write `FixedWindowLimiter(limit, window)`. Time is cut into fixed windows of `window` seconds: window number `t // window`. A user may make at most `limit` allowed requests in each window; the count starts again at 0 in the next window.
levels.sampleInput:
events = [('u1', 1), ('u1', 2), ('u1', 3), ('u1', 4), ('u1', 11), ('u2', 5), ('u1', 12)]
limiter = FixedWindowLimiter(3, 10)
print([limiter.allow(u, t) for u, t in events])
levels.expectedOutput: [True, True, True, False, True, True, True]
edgeCases: A request at t = 10 starts the second window (10 // 10 = 1)
A new user starts with a fresh count

levels.title: Sliding window log
levels.prompt: Write `SlidingWindowLimiter(limit, window)`. A request at time `t` is allowed when fewer than `limit` allowed requests by that user happened in the last `window` seconds, meaning at times `s` with `t - window < s <= t`. Keep a log of each user's allowed request times and drop old entries as time moves on. Rejected requests are not logged.
levels.sampleInput:
events = [('u1', 1), ('u1', 2), ('u1', 3), ('u1', 10), ('u1', 11), ('u1', 12), ('u1', 13), ('u2', 13)]
limiter = SlidingWindowLimiter(3, 10)
print([limiter.allow(u, t) for u, t in events])
levels.expectedOutput: [True, True, True, False, True, True, True, True]
edgeCases: An entry exactly `window` seconds old no longer counts (t - s == window is outside the window)
Pop old entries from the front so each request does O(1) amortized work

levels.title: Token bucket with refill
levels.prompt: Write `TokenBucket(capacity, refill_per_second)`. Each user has a bucket that starts full with `capacity` tokens. Before each request, add `(t - last_time) * refill_per_second` tokens, never going above `capacity`. A request costs 1 token: it is allowed when at least 1 token is available (then 1 is removed), otherwise it is rejected and no token is removed. A user's `last_time` is the time of their previous request, allowed or not (their first request has nothing to refill).
levels.expectedOutput: [True, True, True, False, True, False, True, True, False, True]
edgeCases: Tokens never exceed the capacity, however long the user was idle
Store tokens and last_time per user, not per bucket class
